schemas.codebase_community:
CREATE TABLE badges
(
    Id     INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    UserId INTEGER          null,
    Name   TEXT null,
    Date   DATETIME     null,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE comments
(
    Id              INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    PostId          INTEGER          null,
    Score           INTEGER          null,
    Text            TEXT     null,
    CreationDate    DATETIME     null,
    UserId          INTEGER          null,
    UserDisplayName TEXT null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE postHistory
(
    Id                INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    PostHistoryTypeId INTEGER          null,
    PostId            INTEGER          null,
    RevisionGUID      TEXT null,
    CreationDate      DATETIME     null,
    UserId            INTEGER          null,
    Text              TEXT     null,
    Comment           TEXT         null,
    UserDisplayName   TEXT null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE postLinks
(
    Id            INTEGER      not null
        primary key,
    CreationDate  DATETIME null,
    PostId        INTEGER      null,
    RelatedPostId INTEGER      null,
    LinkTypeId    INTEGER      null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (RelatedPostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE posts
(
    Id                    INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    PostTypeId            INTEGER          null,
    AcceptedAnswerId      INTEGER          null,
    CreaionDate           DATETIME     null,
    Score                 INTEGER          null,
    ViewCount             INTEGER          null,
    Body                  TEXT     null,
    OwnerUserId           INTEGER          null,
    LasActivityDate       DATETIME     null,
    Title                 TEXT null,
    Tags                  TEXT null,
    AnswerCount           INTEGER          null,
    CommentCount          INTEGER          null,
    FavoriteCount         INTEGER          null,
    LastEditorUserId      INTEGER          null,
    LastEditDate          DATETIME     null,
    CommunityOwnedDate    DATETIME    null,
    ParentId              INTEGER          null,
    ClosedDate            DATETIME     null,
    OwnerDisplayName      TEXT null,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT null,
        foreign key (LastEditorUserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (OwnerUserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (ParentId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE tags
(
    Id            INTEGER          not null
        primary key,
    TagName       TEXT null,
    Count         INTEGER          null,
    ExcerptPostId INTEGER          null,
    WikiPostId    INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (ExcerptPostId) references posts (Id)
        on update cascade on delete cascade
);

CREATE TABLE users
(
    Id              INTEGER          not null UNIQUE
        primary key,
    Reputation      INTEGER          null,
    CreationDate    DATETIME     null,
    DisplayName     TEXT null,
    LastAccessDate  DATETIME     null,
    WebsiteUrl      TEXT null,
    Location        TEXT null,
    AboutMe         TEXT     null,
    Views           INTEGER          null,
    UpVotes         INTEGER          null,
    DownVotes       INTEGER          null,
    AccountId       INTEGER          null,
    Age             INTEGER          null,
    ProfileImageUrl TEXT null
);

CREATE TABLE votes
(
    Id           INTEGER  not null
        primary key,
    PostId       INTEGER  null,
    VoteTypeId   INTEGER  null,
    CreationDate DATE null,
    UserId       INTEGER  null,
    BountyAmount INTEGER  null,
        foreign key (PostId) references posts (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade,
        foreign key (UserId) references users (Id)
            on update cascade on delete cascade
);

schemas.financial:
CREATE TABLE account
(
    account_id  INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null,
    frequency   TEXT   not null,
    date        DATE          not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE card
(
    card_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    disp_id INTEGER           not null,
    type    TEXT    not null,
    issued  DATE          not null,
    foreign key (disp_id) references disp (disp_id)
);

CREATE TABLE client
(
    client_id   INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    gender      TEXT not null,
    birth_date  DATE       not null,
    district_id INTEGER        not null,
    foreign key (district_id) references district (district_id)
);

CREATE TABLE disp
(
    disp_id    INTEGER        not null
        primary key,
    client_id  INTEGER        not null,
    account_id INTEGER        not null,
    type      TEXT not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id),
    foreign key (client_id) references client (client_id)
);

CREATE TABLE district
(
    district_id INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    A2          TEXT   not null,
    A3          TEXT   not null,
    A4          TEXT       not null,
    A5          TEXT           not null,
    A6          TEXT           not null,
    A7          TEXT           not null,
    A8          INTEGER        not null,
    A9          INTEGER           not null,
    A10         REAL not null,
    A11         INTEGER           not null,
    A12         REAL null,
    A13         REAL not null,
    A14         INTEGER           not null,
    A15         INTEGER        null,
    A16         INTEGER          not null
);

CREATE TABLE loan
(
    loan_id    INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    date       DATE          not null,
    amount     INTEGER           not null,
    duration   INTEGER           not null,
    payments   REAL not null,
    status     TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE `order`
(
    order_id   INTEGER default 0 not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER           not null,
    bank_to    TEXT    not null,
    account_to INTEGER           not null,
    amount     REAL not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT    not null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE trans
(
    trans_id   INTEGER default 0    not null
        primary key,
    account_id INTEGER default 0    not null,
    date       DATE             not null,
    type       TEXT       not null,
    operation  TEXT      null,
    amount     INTEGER              not null,
    balance    INTEGER             not null,
    k_symbol   TEXT      null,
    bank       TEXT       null,
    account    INTEGER          null,
    foreign key (account_id) references account (account_id)
);

CREATE TABLE `atom` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `element` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `bond` (
  `bond_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `bond_type` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`bond_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `connected` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `atom_id2` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `bond_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`,`atom_id2`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id2`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`bond_id`) REFERENCES `bond` (`bond_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

  PRIMARY KEY (`molecule_id`)

items.question: Please list the lowest three eligible free rates for students aged 5-17 in continuation schools.
items.raw_evidence: Eligible free rates for students aged 5-17 = `Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` / `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`

nodes.name: Eligible free rate for students aged 5-17

items.notes: Anchor example: pure Formula. Both terms ground 1:1 to frpm columns. Useful as the 'happy path' template for Formula nodes.

items.question: Among the schools with an SAT excellence rate of over 0.3, what is the highest eligible free rate for students aged 5-17?
items.raw_evidence: Excellence rate = NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr; Eligible free rates for students aged 5-17 = `Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)` / `Enrollment (Ages 5-17)`

nodes.name: Eligible free rate for students aged 5-17

items.notes: f2 'Eligible free rate' is identical to qid=1's Formula -- argues for a dedup pass when building the L1 graph so one Formula node is shared across all questions that reference it.

items.question: What is the ratio in percentage of Santa Clara County schools that are locally funded compared to all other types of charter school funding?
items.raw_evidence: Ratio in percentage = (count(locally funded schools in Santa Clara) / count(all funding type schools in Santa Clara) * 100%

nodes.name: Locally-funded share of Santa Clara County charter schools
nodes.expression: count(locally funded schools in Santa Clara) / count(all funding-type schools in Santa Clara) * 100

items.notes: SCHEMA GAP: the Formula's expression contains value LITERALS ('locally funded', 'Santa Clara') that need to ground to (column, value) pairs, not bare columns. Worked around by emitting separate ValueMap nodes alongside the Formula. A grounding entry with an optional 'value' field would let one Formula self-contain its filters.

items.question: What is the city location of the high school level school with Lunch Provision 2 whose lowest grade is 9 and the highest grade is 12 in the county of Merced?
items.raw_evidence: High school can be represented as EILCode = 'HS'
items.notes: Anchor example: a single-value mapping is cleanest as Concept -> ValueMap (not Rule). Use Rule when the predicate is a range/composition, not equality to a single value.

items.question: Name all cards with 2015 frame style ranking below 100 on EDHRec.
items.raw_evidence: below 100 on EDHRec refers to EDHRec <100; with 2015 frame style refers to frameVersion = 2015;
items.notes: Anchor example: one BIRD evidence string -> two atoms. Range/inequality => Rule; single-value label => ValueMap.

items.question: Calculate the percentage of the cards availabe in Chinese Simplified.
items.raw_evidence: Chinese Simplified' is the language; percentage = Divide(Sum(id where language = 'Chinese Simplified'), Count(id)) *100

nodes.name: percentage of cards in Chinese Simplified

items.notes: Ambiguous DB target for 'language' -- both foreign_data and set_translations expose it. Chose foreign_data because the question is about cards (per-card translations) rather than set names. Grounding ambiguity is itself a finding for the L1->L2 builder.

items.question: What's the magic card market name for the set which was released on 2017/6/9?
items.raw_evidence: magic card market name refers to mcmName
items.notes: BORDERLINE: pure column-rename evidence. None of Formula/Rule/ValueMap fits cleanly; used Concept with a free-text definition. Strong argument for a 5th node type ('ColumnAlias' / 'Projection') with formal grounding to (table, column).

items.question: What is the language of the "Battlebond" set?
items.raw_evidence: "Battlebond" set refers to name = 'Battlebond'

items.question: What is the title of the post that is owned by csgillespie and has the highest popularity?
items.raw_evidence: "csgillespie" is the DisplayName of user; highest popularity refers to Max(ViewCount)

items.question: Among posts by Harvey Motulsky and Noah Snyder, which one has higher popularity?
items.raw_evidence: Has higher popularity means the post has higher view count ; calculation = MAX(SUM(ViewCount)) where DisplayName = 'Harvey Motulsky' OR DisplayName = 'Noah Snyder';

nodes.name: higher popularity = MAX(SUM(ViewCount)) per user
nodes.expression: MAX(SUM(ViewCount)) WHERE DisplayName = 'Harvey Motulsky' OR DisplayName = 'Noah Snyder'

items.notes: Same SCHEMA GAP as qid=65: Formula expression embeds value literals; ValueMaps emitted alongside.

items.question: How many tags have post count between 5,000 to 7,000?
items.raw_evidence: post count between 5,000 to 7,000 refers to Count BETWEEN 5000 and 7000;

items.question: Which of the three segments—SME, LAM and KAM—has the biggest and lowest percentage increases in consumption paid in EUR between 2012 and 2013?
items.raw_evidence: Increase or Decrease = consumption for 2013 - consumption for 2012; Percentage of Increase = (Increase or Decrease / consumption for 2013) * 100%; The first 4 strings of the Date values in the yearmonth table can represent year

nodes.name: Increase or Decrease in consumption (2013 vs 2012)

items.notes: SCHEMA GAP: f1/f2 implicitly depend on r1's date-parsing convention (the 2012/2013 split is realized via SUBSTR over yearmonth.Date). The current schema has no formal Formula->Rule 'depends_on' edge -- the dependency lives only in the annotator's head.

items.question: How many transactions were paid in CZK in the morning of 2012/8/26?
items.raw_evidence: '2012/8/26' can be represented by '2012-08-26'; The morning refers to the time before '13:00:00'
items.notes: r1 is really an INPUT-NORMALIZATION hint ('2012/8/26' from the user maps to '2012-08-26' in the DB), not a business Rule. SCHEMA GAP: a 'FormatHint' / 'InputNormalization' node would be a cleaner home for this.

items.question: What is the amount spent by customer "38508" at the gas stations? How much had the customer spent in January 2012?
items.raw_evidence: January 2012 refers to the Date value = '201201'

items.question: Which are the top five best selling products? Please state the full name of them.
items.raw_evidence: Description of products contains full name
items.notes: BORDERLINE: column-rename, same gap as qid=491.

items.question: Give the name of the league had the most matches end as draw in the 2016 season?
items.raw_evidence: most matches end as draw refers to MAX(SUM(home_team_goal = away_team_goal)); 2016 season refers to season = '2015/2016';

nodes.name: most matches ending as a draw

items.notes: v1 is a non-obvious user-input->DB-value mapping ('2016 season' -> '2015/2016'). Pure ValueMap fits.

items.question: Give the team_fifa_api_id of teams with more than 50 but less than 60 build-up play speed.
items.raw_evidence: teams with more than 50 but less than 60 build-up play speed refers to buildUpPlaySpeed >50 AND buildUpPlaySpeed <60;

nodes.name: build-up play speed strictly between 50 and 60

items.question: Among all the players whose weight is under 130, how many of them preferred foot in attacking is left?
items.raw_evidence: weight < 130; preferred foot in attacking refers to preferred_foot; preferred_foot = 'left';
items.notes: c1 is a column-rename (BORDERLINE, same gap as qid=491). 'attacking' in the user phrase is decorative here -- preferred_foot has nothing to do with attacking specifically.

items.question: State the district and region for loan ID '4990'.
items.raw_evidence: A2, A3 contains the information about district and region respectively.
items.notes: BORDERLINE: pure column-rename for opaque column names. The financial DB's A2..A16 are cryptic -- this kind of evidence is the strongest argument that knowledge-augmented T2SQL is necessary (no LLM can guess that A3 = region from the schema alone).

items.question: Who are the female account holders who own credit cards and also have loans?
items.raw_evidence: Female refers to gender = 'F'

items.question: How many clients who choose statement of weekly issuance are Owner?
items.raw_evidence: Frequency = 'POPLATEK TYDNE' refers to weekly issuance

items.question: Provide the IDs and age of the client with high level credit card, which is eligible for loans.
items.raw_evidence: the credit card is high-level refers to card.type = 'gold'; eligible for loans refers to disp.type = 'OWNER'
items.notes: Note: 'eligible for loans' is annotated as ValueMap on disp.type='OWNER', but the SEMANTIC link (only OWNERs can apply for loans) is a business RULE that happens to project to a single column value. ValueMap captures the surface mapping but not the underlying rule -- the L1 graph may want both nodes joined by a 'realized_as' edge.

items.question: Please calculate the race completion percentage of Japanese drivers from 2007 to 2009.
items.raw_evidence: from 2007 to 2009 refers to year between 2007 and 2009; race completion refers to time is not null; percentage = Divide(COUNT(DriverID where time is not null and year between 2007 and 2009),Count (DriverID where year between 2007 and 2009))*100;

nodes.name: race completion percentage
nodes.expression: COUNT(DriverID WHERE time IS NOT NULL AND year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009) / COUNT(DriverID WHERE year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009) * 100

items.notes: Formula f1 reuses both rules r1 (year filter) and r2 (completion definition). No 'depends_on' edge in current schema -- same gap as qid=1482.

items.question: Which race has the shortest actual finishing time? Please give the name and year.
items.raw_evidence: shortest actual finishing time refers to Min(milliseconds) except milliseconds = null;

nodes.name: min milliseconds excluding null
nodes.expression: MIN(milliseconds) WHERE milliseconds IS NOT NULL

items.question: How many times the circuits were held in Austria? Please give their location and coordinates.
items.raw_evidence: location coordinates refers to (lat,lng); Austria refers to country = 'Austria';
items.notes: SCHEMA GAP: c1 maps a concept to a column TUPLE, not a single column. Concept has no formal multi-column grounding; used 'definition' free-text. Same pattern at qid=1364.

items.question: What was the longest time a driver had ever spent at a pit stop?
items.raw_evidence: longest time spent at pitstop refers to MAX(duration)

nodes.name: longest time spent at pit stop

items.question: What is the total budgeted amount for all category in "October Speaker" event?
items.raw_evidence: total budgeted amount refers to SUM(amount) where event_name = 'October Speaker'

nodes.name: total budgeted amount for an event

items.notes: Cross-table predicate (budget.amount filtered by event.event_name via budget.link_to_event = event.event_id) -- join path is implicit in the Formula. The L1 builder will need to surface JOIN paths from foreign keys.

items.question: How many cities are there in Orange County, Virginia?
items.raw_evidence: Orange County is the county name, Virginia is the state name
items.notes: BORDERLINE: parses an ambiguous user-input string ('Orange County, Virginia') into two (column, value) bindings. ValueMap captures the surface mapping, but the act of *parsing* the input string isn't itself a node type -- arguably a 'ParseHint' role.

items.question: Where is Amy Firth's hometown?
items.raw_evidence: hometown refers to city, county, state
items.notes: SCHEMA GAP: multi-column projection again (same as qid=978).

items.question: What is the category of event which was taken place in 2020-03-24T12:00:00?
items.raw_evidence: taken place in 2020-03-24T12:00:00 refers to event_date = '2020-03-24T12:00:00'
items.notes: Could be ValueMap (single value of a single column), but used as a filter; Rule fits more idiomatically. Either is defensible -- annotator-judgment edge case worth documenting.

items.question: What is the eye clolour of the heaviest superhero?
items.raw_evidence: the heaviest superhero refers to MAX(weight_kg); eye colour refers to colour where eye_colour_id = colour.id;

nodes.name: eye colour
nodes.definition: JOIN superhero.eye_colour_id = colour.id, then project colour.colour

items.notes: SCHEMA GAP: c2 encodes a JOIN-PATH ('to read eye colour you must traverse FK eye_colour_id -> colour.id'), not a column rename or value. Yet another argument for a 'PathConcept' node type that exposes (start_table, fk, end_table.column).

items.question: Which superhero has the most durability published by Dark Horse Comics?
items.raw_evidence: which superhero refers to superhero_name; most durability refers to MAX(attribute_value) WHERE attribute_name = 'durability'; published by Dark Horse Comics refers to publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics';
items.notes: BIRD evidence uses 'durability' (lowercase) here but 'Strength' (initcap) at qid=786 -- KB needs explicit case-folding / canonicalization policy. f1 carries value literal in expression (same gap as qid=65).

items.question: Provide the hero name and race of Charles Chandler.
items.raw_evidence: hero name refers to superhero_name; Charles Chandler is the full name of superhero;
items.notes: Mix of one column-alias Concept (c1) and one ValueMap (v1) -- shows the two patterns naturally coexist in a single evidence.

items.question: How many heroes have the highest attribute value in strength?
items.raw_evidence: highest attribute value in strength refers to MAX(attribute_value) WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength';
items.notes: Case mismatch vs qid=769 (see notes there).

items.question: List ID, sex and date of birth of patient whose total protein (TP) below the lower range of the normal index.
items.raw_evidence: total protein (TP) below the lower range of the normal index refers to TP < 6.0

items.question: List all outpatient within normal range of creatinine phosphokinase. Give me the distinct ids.
items.raw_evidence: outpatient refers to Admission = '-'; normal range of creatinine phosphokinase refers to CPK < 250;

items.question: Provide ID, sex and age of patient who has blood glucose (GLU) not within normal range but with total cholesterol(T-CHO) within normal range.
items.raw_evidence: age = SUBTRACT(year(current_timestamp), year(Birthday)); blood glucose (GLU) not within normal range refers to GLU > = 180; total cholesterol(T-CHO) within normal range refers to `T-CHO` < 250;
items.notes: BIRD evidence couples 'GLU not within normal range' to 'GLU >= 180' -- the rule encodes an ABOVE-normal condition; the Concept name has to preserve polarity. A literal paraphrase like 'GLU normal range' would flip the SQL.

items.question: How many elements are there for single bond molecules?
items.raw_evidence: single bond refers to bond_type = '-';

items.question: Calculate the percentage of carcinogenic molecules which contain the Chlorine element.
items.raw_evidence: label = '+' mean molecules are carcinogenic; percentage = DIVIDE(SUM(label = '+' and element = 'cl'), COUNT(molecule_id)) as percentage

nodes.name: percentage of carcinogenic molecules containing Chlorine

items.notes: Two value-literal patterns inside one Formula expression -- same column-value-in-expression gap as qid=65.

items.question: What is the total number of molecules with double bonded oxygen?
items.raw_evidence: oxygen refers to element = 'o'; double bond refers to bond_type = ' = ';
items.notes: BIRD evidence shows the value as ' = ' with surrounding whitespace; the actual DB value is '='. Notes the need for a whitespace-normalization step in the KB ingestor.
